package_info.package_versions: 2.3.5 and earlier (as referenced in the Equifax breach context)
package_info.why_malicious: The report discusses the exploitation of a known vulnerability (CVE-2017-5638) in outdated versions of the Apache Struts open source component. Attackers leveraged this vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to sensitive data in the Equifax breach. The maliciousness arises from the use of a vulnerable library version in production systems, which enables remote code execution by attackers.

execution_context.trigger: When the vulnerable Apache Struts library processes a specially crafted HTTP request containing a malicious Content-Type header
execution_context.file_location: struts-core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/Dispatcher.java (within the vulnerable version of Apache Struts)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon receiving an HTTP request, the code evaluates the Content-Type header using OGNL expression evaluation, allowing attacker-supplied expressions to be executed on the server, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code evaluates user-supplied HTTP headers as OGNL expressions, which allows attackers to inject and execute arbitrary code on the server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, HTTP headers should be treated as untrusted input and never directly evaluated as code. The vulnerable code path fails to properly sanitize or restrict OGNL evaluation, violating secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of OGNL in Struts is for safe expression evaluation within the application context, not for evaluating untrusted HTTP headers. Evaluating headers as code is never legitimate.
key_indicators: OGNL expression evaluation on HTTP headers
Lack of input sanitization on Content-Type header
Direct invocation of evaluateOGNL or similar methods on user-controlled data

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request with a malicious Content-Type header to the vulnerable Apache Struts endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggering the vulnerable code path in the Struts library.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code in Apache Struts evaluates the malicious OGNL expression from the Content-Type header.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the application server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized access to sensitive data or further compromises the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration or further lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Detection of OGNL expression evaluation on HTTP headers, especially Content-Type
Unusual or unexpected Content-Type header values in HTTP requests
Execution of system commands or abnormal process creation by the web server process
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable Apache Struts library versions (e.g., struts2-core-2.3.5.jar) in application dependencies
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with Content-Type headers containing OGNL payloads (e.g., ${...})
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement software composition analysis (SCA) to identify and alert on known-vulnerable versions of Apache Struts in application dependencies. Monitor HTTP traffic for suspicious Content-Type headers containing OGNL expressions. Correlate web server logs for unexpected command execution or process creation following such requests. Automated detection should flag applications using affected Struts versions and alert on inbound requests with OGNL payloads in headers.
